q: A law fixing minimum wages is challenged as violating equality and freedom, the State pleading the directive shield. Which statement is correct?
options: The plea fails: the shield covers two specified directives, and wages is not one
The plea succeeds: the shield covers any law advancing a Directive Principle
The plea fails: the shield operates only against the freedom guarantee
The plea succeeds: wage legislation falls within the resource directives
expl: The shield is confined to two clauses, and a minimum wage law does not fall within them.
why: The fourth option attempts to force the law into the covered directives, which is the more sophisticated route to the wrong answer.
trapnote: Do not merely ask whether the shield exists. Ask whether this law falls inside its two clauses.

q: An owner argues that the 2024 ruling permits acquisition of any flat without compensation, as all private property is now a community resource. Which statement is correct?
options: The argument is correct, the ruling having widened the directive to all property
The argument fails because the directive was deleted by the same ruling
The argument is correct only where the State declares a public purpose
The argument inverts the ruling, which held that not all private resources qualify
expl: The ruling narrowed the directive; ownership alone is not the test.
why: The fourth option concedes the premise and adds a condition, which makes it the most plausible of the wrong answers.
trapnote: When a ruling narrows a provision, expect the exam to test it through an option that widens it.

q: Consider a claim that a citizen may be prosecuted directly for breach of a Fundamental Duty: 1-No writ lies to enforce a duty. 2-Prosecution requires an enabling statute. 3-A duty may inform the interpretation of a restriction on a right. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: All three are correct; duties operate through statute and interpretation, not directly.
why: The third statement is the one candidates doubt: duties have been used to sustain the reasonableness of restrictions.
trapnote: Duties have indirect legal force. Their absence of direct enforceability does not make them decorative.

q: An accused from a Scheduled Area is produced without counsel. Which combination states the correct obligations?
options: Arrange free aid only if he applies in writing to the legal services authority
Inform him of the right, arrange free aid and record the fact in the case diary
Arrange free aid only after the charge has been framed by the trial court
Inform him of the right, the arrangement of aid resting with the trial court alone
expl: The obligation arises at the earliest stage and is not contingent on a written application.
why: Each wrong option defers or conditions the obligation, which is how the safeguard is most often defeated in practice.
trapnote: Liberty safeguards attach at the earliest stage. Options that postpone them are usually wrong.

q: A State pleads that a directive obliges it to provide housing and that no budgetary provision is therefore needed. Which statement is correct?
options: A directive guides policy and is implemented through law and budget, not by itself
A directive creates an immediate obligation enforceable without any legislation
A directive has no role once the State has framed any housing scheme at all
A directive operates only where the State expressly adopts it by resolution
expl: Directives set goals; implementation requires legislative and financial action.
why: The second option overstates directives into self-executing obligations, the opposite error to treating them as irrelevant.
trapnote: A directive is a goal, not a self-executing command. Implementation runs through law and budget.

q: Consider: 1-The legal aid directive is in the socialist group. 2-The monuments directive is in the Gandhian group. 3-The weaker sections directive is in the Gandhian group. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Monuments belongs to the liberal group; legal aid is socialist and weaker sections Gandhian.
why: Two Gandhian-sounding items are placed together so that a candidate grouping by intuition rather than by list will take both.
trapnote: Group assignment questions reward learning the three lists as blocks rather than item by item.

q: A magistrate declines to provide counsel to an indigent accused to save public expenditure. Which statement is correct?
options: The trial stands, legal aid being a directive and therefore unenforceable
The trial stands if the accused did not ask for counsel at the first hearing
The trial is vitiated, free legal aid being a component of a fair procedure
The trial is vitiated only where the offence carries a sentence of death
expl: Denial of legal aid to an indigent accused vitiates the trial as an unfair procedure.
why: The fourth option confines a general safeguard to capital cases, which is a common and plausible narrowing.
trapnote: Safeguards attaching to fair procedure are not confined to the gravest offences.

q: Consider the claim that Directive Principles authorise the police to prohibit any assembly said to disturb welfare. Which statement is correct?
options: The claim succeeds: directives are fundamental in the governance of the country
The claim fails: a restriction still needs a law and a listed ground
The claim succeeds where the State records that welfare is advanced
The claim fails: directives have no relevance to restrictions on rights
expl: A directive cannot supply a ground of restriction that the Constitution does not list.
why: The fourth option reaches the right result by denying directives any relevance, which is itself wrong.
trapnote: Right answer, wrong reason is still wrong. Directives are relevant, but cannot create new grounds.

q: A scheme provides free education to children below six and none for those aged six to fourteen. Which statement is correct?
options: The six to fourteen group holds a fundamental right, which the omission breaches
Both groups hold directives only, and the scheme is a matter of policy
Both groups hold fundamental rights, and the scheme breaches both of them
The below-six group holds a fundamental right, which the scheme satisfies
expl: Six to fourteen is a right; below six is a directive on early childhood care.
why: The fourth option reverses the two categories, which is the error the 2002 amendment most commonly produces.
trapnote: One amendment split this subject by age. Six to fourteen is the right; below six remained a directive.

q: A case involves child labour, unequal wages, denial of legal aid and acquisition of homes. Which statement correctly describes the applicable framework?
options: Four directives, each enforceable only through legislation enacted for the purpose
Four fundamental rights, each directly enforceable by petition to a High Court
Two rights and two directives, the directives being wholly outside judicial notice
A right, a directive, a directive read into a right, and a directive with a narrow shield
expl: Child labour is a right; wages a directive; legal aid a directive read into a right; acquisition engages the shielded directives.
why: Synthesis questions of this kind punish uniform characterisation. The four limbs sit in three different legal categories.
trapnote: In a four-limb scenario the limbs rarely share one category. Classify each separately.
